_: One list, read by both type.html and index.html. Adding a face here puts it in the picker and makes its ?type= link work. spec is the Google css2 family string: axes alphabetical, lowercase before uppercase, or the request 400s.

display.name: Bodoni Moda
display.note: what is on the site now. Didone, hairline thins, fashion plate

display.name: Instrument Serif
display.note: narrow and light, a lot of air. Reads current without trying

display.name: Fraunces
display.note: has a WONK axis that tilts the terminals off true. Drag it

display.name: Newsreader
display.note: editorial, even colour, built to be read rather than looked at

display.name: Cormorant Garamond
display.note: very fine, old-style. Goes delicate at this size

display.name: Italiana
display.note: deco capitals, gallery signage. Almost no weight to it

display.name: Gloock
display.note: heavy Didone, thick thins. Loud where Bodoni is sharp

display.name: Libre Caslon Display
display.note: Caslon cut for headlines, slightly bookish

display.name: Playfair Display
display.note: the familiar one. Safe, and everyone has seen it

display.name: DM Serif Display
display.note: compact, high contrast, solid on a white field

display.name: Spectral
display.note: low contrast serif, quiet, holds up small as well as large

display.name: Syne
display.note: geometric and odd, art-world sans. Breaks the serif assumption

display.name: Space Grotesk
display.note: technical sans, agrees with the instrument frame

display.name: Bricolage Grotesque
display.note: contemporary grotesque with irregular joints

display.name: Shrikhand
display.note: fat, syrupy, brush logic. Named after the dessert

display.name: Rozha One
display.note: Didone contrast run through Devanagari construction. Closest thing here to Bodoni with a different accent

display.name: Yatra One
display.note: brush drawn, uneven stroke, a lot of personality in the l and the a

display.name: Khand
display.note: condensed and angular. Signage, not literature

display.name: Anek Devanagari
display.note: variable width and weight. Squeeze it

display.name: Tiro Devanagari Hindi
display.note: formal text face, properly cut, no gimmick. The sober option in this group

display.name: Rubik Glitch
display.note: scanline tearing frozen mid-frame

display.name: Rubik Broken Fax
display.note: fed through a machine that gave up halfway

display.name: Rubik Distressed
display.note: eaten away at the edges, which is exactly what the artwork on the page is doing

display.name: Rubik Moonrocks
display.note: porous, cratered, lit from one side

display.name: Rubik Wet Paint
display.note: still running down the wall

display.name: Rubik Scribble
display.note: filled in by hand with a biro, badly and on purpose

display.name: Rubik Marker Hatch
display.note: hatched with a marker, open counters

display.name: Lacquer
display.note: spray paint through a stencil, overspray left in

display.name: Sixtyfour
display.note: a CRT you can bleed and scan with two axes. Push BLED

display.name: Workbench
display.note: blueprint plotter. Same two axes, colder result

display.name: Doto
display.note: dot matrix. ROND turns the dots from squares to circles

display.name: Major Mono Display
display.note: lowercase only, monospaced, reads as a label printer

display.name: Micro 5
display.note: drawn to stay legible at five pixels. Absurd at this size, excellent at eight

display.name: Silkscreen
display.note: bitmap, hard pixels, no anti-aliasing in its bones

display.name: Jacquard 12
display.note: woven on a loom grid. Blackletter crossed with a punch card

display.name: Nabla
display.note: an actual colour font. Chromatic 3D extrusion, ignores the black ink of the page

display.name: Honk
display.note: colour font, fairground. MORF bends it

display.name: Rampart One
display.note: puffed up and outlined, like it was inflated

display.name: Monoton
display.note: concentric lines inside every stroke. Deco neon

display.name: Bungee Shade
display.note: signage with a hard cast shadow built into the glyph

display.name: Kumar One Outline
display.note: outline only, Devanagari lineage, very loud

display.name: Moirai One
display.note: op art. The strokes interfere with themselves

display.name: Climate Crisis
display.note: one axis, YEAR, and the letters melt as you move through time. Drag it to 2050

display.name: Megrim
display.note: hairline geometry, drafting compass. Nearly disappears

display.name: Codystar
display.note: marquee bulbs, dotted. A cinema front in 1972

display.name: Londrina Sketch
display.note: scratched out fast with a dry pen

display.name: Syncopate
display.note: spaced so wide the name stops being a word and becomes a row

display.name: Sankofa Display
display.note: Adinkra influenced, sharp joints, unusual proportions

mono.name: JetBrains Mono
mono.note: what is on the site now. Even, engineered, wide apertures

mono.name: IBM Plex Mono
mono.note: warmer, slight slab. Corporate in a good way

mono.name: Space Mono
mono.note: quirky, 1960s terminal. More character, less neutral

mono.name: DM Mono
mono.note: light and narrow, the quietest of these

mono.name: Martian Mono
mono.note: very wide, heavily spaced. Labels become structure

mono.name: Azeret Mono
mono.note: blunt and square, closest to a plotter

mono.name: Micro 5
mono.note: built for five pixels, so at eight it is genuinely strange and genuinely legible

mono.name: Silkscreen
mono.note: hard bitmap. Every label becomes a readout

mono.name: Major Mono Display
mono.note: lowercase only, so the uppercase labels come out as small forms

mono.name: Doto
mono.note: dot matrix at label size. Dense and strange

mono.name: Workbench
mono.note: plotter output. Agrees with the frame and the tick marks

mono.name: Jacquard 12
mono.note: woven grid. Unreadable at eight pixels, probably. Worth seeing
